# T2: Ledger.remove refuses to overdraw

Make stocklib.ledger.Ledger.remove raise ValueError when asked to remove more than the quantity in stock for that SKU (an unknown SKU has 0 in stock). A refused removal must leave the stock unchanged. Removing exactly the quantity in stock is allowed and leaves 0.
------
diff --git a/stocklib/ledger.py b/stocklib/ledger.py
index 6dd554f..a30914e 100644
--- a/stocklib/ledger.py
+++ b/stocklib/ledger.py
@@ -13,7 +13,10 @@ class Ledger:
     def remove(self, sku, qty):
         if qty <= 0:
             raise ValueError("qty to remove must be positive")
-        self._stock[sku] = self._stock.get(sku, 0) - qty
+        in_stock = self._stock.get(sku, 0)
+        if qty > in_stock:
+            raise ValueError("qty to remove exceeds quantity in stock")
+        self._stock[sku] = in_stock - qty
 
     def quantity(self, sku):
         return self._stock.get(sku, 0)

content.text:
The change makes `Ledger.remove` raise `ValueError` when `qty` is more than the quantity in stock. An unknown SKU counts as 0 in stock, so any removal from it is refused. The check runs before the stock dict is written, so a refused removal leaves the stock unchanged. Removing exactly the quantity in stock passes the check and leaves 0. The existing positive-quantity check is unchanged, and the diff touches nothing else. I reviewed this from the task statement and the diff alone. I didn't build the code or run any tests.
